title: When too much turns bitter
literal_meaning: If you squeeze a lemon too much, it turns bitter.
explanation: The useful action—extracting juice—becomes counterproductive when carried too far. The warning is about proportion: pressing for one more favour, one more concession or one more advantage may damage what was already achieved. It does not mean that effort itself is bad.
meaning_odia: ଲେମ୍ବୁରୁ ରସ ପାଇବାକୁ ଚିପୁଡ଼ିବା ଦରକାର, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅତି କଲେ ସ୍ୱାଦ ବିଗିଡ଼ିଯାଏ—ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ କଥାଟିର ମର୍ମ ଅଛି। ଯେଉଁ ଚେଷ୍ଟା ପ୍ରଥମେ ଉପକାର କରୁଥିଲା, ମାତ୍ରା ଛାଡ଼ିଲେ ସେହି ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଓଲଟା ଫଳ ଦେଇପାରେ। ତେଣୁ କେବେ ଆଉ ଟିକେ କରିବା ଓ କେବେ ଅଟକିବା, ସେହି ବିଚାର ମୁଖ୍ୟ; ପରିଶ୍ରମ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବା ଏହାର ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: After a neighbour has agreed to help for an afternoon, repeatedly asking for more time may invite this saying. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The image makes a social judgement through an ordinary kitchen action. This reading explains the metaphor; it is not a scientific claim about every citrus fruit or a documented account of how the proverb originated.

odia_summary: ଅତି କଲେ ଭଲ କାମର ଫଳ ମଧ୍ୟ ଖରାପ ହୋଇପାରେ।
english_summary: Pressing a useful action too far can spoil its result; the warning is about proportion, not effort itself.
